sanskrit: uccāvacaṃ balaṃ jñātvā madhyasthaṃ cāpi bhārata prahṛṣṭam aprahṛṣṭaṃ ca saṃdadhāma tathā paraiḥ
english: Having assessed the forces as high, middling, or low, O Bharata, and knowing who is pleased and who is not, let us then make peace with our enemies accordingly.

sanskrit: sāmnā bhedena dānena daṇḍena balikarmaṇā nyāyenānamya ca parān balāc cānamya durbalān
english: Through conciliation, through sowing discord, through gifts, through chastisement, through tribute — bring the powerful to submission by righteous means, and bend the weak by force.

sanskrit: sāntvayitvā ca mitrāṇi balaṃ cābhāṣyatāṃ sukham sakośabalasaṃvṛddhaḥ samyak siddhim avāpsyasi
english: Having appeased your allies and encouraged the army with reassurance, you, grown strong with treasury and forces, will properly achieve success.

sanskrit: yotsyase cāpi balibhir aribhiḥ pratyupasthitaiḥ anyais tvaṃ pāṇḍavair vāpi hīnasvabalavāhanaiḥ
english: You will have to fight against powerful enemies who are arrayed before you — whether others or the Pāṇḍavas themselves — even if they are reduced in their own forces and vehicles.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvaṃ viniścitya vyavasāyaṃ svadharmataḥ yathākālaṃ manuṣyendra ciraṃ sukham avāpsyasi
english: Having resolved upon all this and applying your effort according to your own duty, O lord of men, you will long enjoy happiness at the right moment.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca atha rājā trigartānāṃ suśarmā rathayūthapaḥ prāptakālam idaṃ vākyam uvāca tvarito bhṛśam
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Then Suśarmā, king of the Trigārtas, lord of chariot-hosts, hurriedly spoke these timely words with great urgency.

sanskrit: asakṛn nikṛtaḥ pūrvaṃ matsyaiḥ sālveyakaiḥ saha sūtena caiva matsyasya kīcakena punaḥ punaḥ
english: "I have been wronged again and again — first by the Matsyas together with the Sālveyas, and time and again by Kīcaka, the commander of Matsya's forces.

sanskrit: bādhito bandhubhiḥ sārdhaṃ balād balavatā vibho sa karṇam abhyudīkṣyātha duryodhanam abhāṣata
english: Harassed together with my kinsmen by one mighty through force, O lord" — thus saying, he glanced at Karṇa and then addressed Duryodhana.

sanskrit: asakṛn matsyarājñā me rāṣṭraṃ bādhitam ojasā praṇetā kīcakaś cāsya balavān abhavat purā
english: "My kingdom has been oppressed time and again by the king of Matsya with might, and Kīcaka was his mighty commander-in-chief in former times.

sanskrit: krūro 'marṣī sa duṣṭātmā bhuvi prakhyātavikramaḥ nihatas tatra gandharvaiḥ pāpakarmā nṛśaṃsavān
english: That cruel, wrathful, evil-souled one, renowned throughout the earth for his valor, that wicked and brutal man was slain there by the Gandharvas.

sanskrit: tasmiṃś ca nihate rājan hīnadarpo nirāśrayaḥ bhaviṣyati nirutsāho virāṭa iti me matiḥ
english: And with him slain, O king, Virāṭa will be stripped of his pride and support, and will be without courage — so is my conviction.

sanskrit: tatra yātrā mama matā yadi te rocate 'nagha kauravāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ karṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: An expedition there is what I have in mind, if it pleases you, O sinless one, and all the Kauravas, and the great-souled Karṇa.

sanskrit: etat prāptam ahaṃ manye kāryam ātyayikaṃ hitam rāṣṭraṃ tasyābhiyātv āśu bahudhānyasamākulam
english: This I consider a task that is both urgent and beneficial — let us swiftly march upon his kingdom, so abundant in grain.

sanskrit: ādadāmo 'sya ratnāni vividhāni vasūni ca grāmān rāṣṭrāṇi vā tasya hariṣyāmo vibhāgaśaḥ
english: Let us carry off his many and various gems and riches, or we shall plunder his villages and territories in division.

sanskrit: atha vā gosahasrāṇi bahūni ca śubhāni ca vividhāni hariṣyāmaḥ pratipīḍya puraṃ balāt
english: Or else we shall seize many thousands of fine cattle of various kinds, pressing upon his city by force.

sanskrit: kauravaiḥ saha saṃgamya trigartaiś ca viśāṃ pate gās tasyāpaharāmāśu saha sarvaiḥ susaṃhatāḥ
english: Uniting with the Kauravas and the Trigārtas, O lord of the people, let us all together swiftly drive away his cattle, well-assembled in force.

sanskrit: saṃdhiṃ vā tena kṛtvā tu nibadhnīmo 'sya pauruṣam hatvā cāsya camūṃ kṛtsnāṃ vaśam anvānayāmahe
english: Or having made a treaty with him, let us restrain his manhood; or having slaughtered his entire army, let us bring him under our dominion.

sanskrit: taṃ vaśe nyāyataḥ kṛtvā sukhaṃ vatsyāmahe vayam bhavato balavṛddhiś ca bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: Having brought him under rightful subjection, we shall dwell in ease, and your strength will increase beyond all doubt."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya karṇo rājānam abravīt sūktaṃ suśarmaṇā vākyaṃ prāptakālaṃ hitaṃ ca naḥ
english: Hearing these words of his, Karṇa said to the king: "What Suśarmā has spoken is well-said — timely and beneficial to us.

sanskrit: tasmāt kṣipraṃ viniryāmo yojayitvā varūthinīm vibhajya cāpy anīkāni yathā vā manyase 'nagha
english: Therefore let us set out quickly, having marshaled the army and arrayed the divisions as you see fit, O sinless one.

sanskrit: prajñāvān kuruvṛddho 'yaṃ sarveṣāṃ naḥ pitāmahaḥ ācāryaś ca tathā droṇaḥ kṛpaḥ śāradvatas tathā
english: This wise elder of the Kurus, our grandsire Bhīṣma, and the preceptor Droṇa, and Kṛpa the son of Śaradwat —

sanskrit: manyante te yathā sarve tathā yātrā vidhīyatām saṃmantrya cāśu gacchāmaḥ sādhanārthaṃ mahīpateḥ
english: — as all of them think fit, so let the expedition be arranged; and having deliberated quickly, let us march to achieve the king's purpose.

sanskrit: kiṃ ca naḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ kāryaṃ hīnārthabalapauruṣaiḥ atyarthaṃ vā pranaṣṭās te prāptā vāpi yamakṣayam
english: And what business do we have with the Pāṇḍavas, diminished in wealth, strength, and valor? They are either utterly lost, or else they have reached the realm of Yama."

sanskrit: yāmo rājann anudvignā virāṭaviṣayaṃ vayam ādāsyāmo hi gās tasya vividhāni vasūni ca
english: "Let us go, O king, without anxiety, into the territory of Virāṭa; we shall take his cattle and various other riches."

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā vākyam ādāya tasya tat vaikartanasya karṇasya kṣipram ājñāpayat svayam
english: Then king Duryodhana, accepting that word of Karṇa, son of Vikartana, himself gave the command swiftly.

sanskrit: śāsane nityasaṃyuktaṃ duḥśāsanam anantaram saha vṛddhais tu saṃmantrya kṣipraṃ yojaya vāhinīm
english: "Duḥśāsana, ever devoted to my command, consult with the elders immediately and then quickly marshal the army.

sanskrit: yathoddeśaṃ ca gacchāmaḥ sahitāḥ sarvakauravaiḥ suśarmā tu yathoddiṣṭaṃ deśaṃ yātu mahārathaḥ
english: We shall march to the designated place together with all the Kauravas; and let the great warrior Suśarmā proceed to the assigned territory.

sanskrit: trigartaiḥ sahito rājā samagrabalavāhanaḥ prāg eva hi susaṃvīto matsyasya viṣayaṃ prati
english: The king, together with the Trigārtas and with his full complement of forces and vehicles, well-guarded, shall go first into Matsya's territory.

sanskrit: jaghanyato vayaṃ tatra yāsyāmo divasāntaram viṣayaṃ matsyarājasya susamṛddhaṃ susaṃhatāḥ
english: We shall follow in the rear a day later, marching in a solid body into the well-prosperous territory of the king of Matsya.

sanskrit: te yātvā sahasā tatra virāṭanagaraṃ prati kṣipraṃ gopān samāsādya gṛhṇantu vipulaṃ dhanam
english: Going quickly toward Virāṭa's city, let them swiftly fall upon the herdsmen there and seize great wealth.

sanskrit: gavāṃ śatasahasrāṇi śrīmanti guṇavanti ca vayam api nigṛhṇīmo dvidhā kṛtvā varūthinīm
english: Hundreds of thousands of cattle, fine and of good quality — these too we shall seize, dividing our army in two.

sanskrit: sa sma gatvā yathoddiṣṭāṃ diśaṃ vahner mahīpatiḥ ādatta gāḥ suśarmātha gharmapakṣasya saptamīm
english: And so, going in the assigned direction of the fire — the southwest — that lord of earth Suśarmā seized the cattle on the seventh day of the fortnight of heat.

sanskrit: aparaṃ divasaṃ sarve rājan saṃbhūya kauravāḥ aṣṭamyāṃ tāny agṛhṇanta gokulāni sahasraśaḥ
english: The next day, O king, all the Kauravas assembled together and on the eighth day seized those herds of cattle by the thousands.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas teṣāṃ mahārāja tatraivāmitatejasām chadmaliṅgapraviṣṭānāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Then, O great king, for those great-souled Pāṇḍavas of immeasurable splendor who had entered there in disguise —

sanskrit: vyatītaḥ samayaḥ samyag vasatāṃ vai purottame kurvatāṃ tasya karmāṇi virāṭasya mahīpateḥ
english: — the agreed period had fully elapsed while they dwelt in that best of cities, performing the services of that lord of earth, Virāṭa.

sanskrit: tatas trayodaśasyānte tasya varṣasya bhārata suśarmaṇā gṛhītaṃ tu godhanaṃ tarasā bahu
english: Then, O Bhārata, at the close of that thirteenth year, the great cattle-wealth was seized by force by Suśarmā.

sanskrit: tato javena mahatā gopāḥ puram athāvrajat apaśyan matsyarājaṃ ca rathāt praskandya kuṇḍalī
english: Then with great speed a herdsman came to the city; and having leapt down from his chariot, his earrings swinging, he approached the king of Matsya.

sanskrit: śūraiḥ parivṛtaṃ yodhaiḥ kuṇḍalāṅgadadhāribhiḥ sadbhiś ca mantribhiḥ sārdhaṃ pāṇḍavaiś ca nararṣabhaiḥ
english: He saw the king surrounded by brave warriors wearing earrings and armlets, and together with noble ministers and the bull-like Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: taṃ sabhāyāṃ mahārājam āsīnaṃ rāṣṭravardhanam so 'bravīd upasaṃgamya virāṭaṃ praṇatas tadā
english: Approaching Virāṭa, that great king seated in the assembly hall, increaser of the kingdom, he spoke with a bow.

sanskrit: asmān yudhi vinirjitya paribhūya sabāndhavān gavāṃ śatasahasrāṇi trigartāḥ kālayanti te tān parīpsa manuṣyendra mā neśuḥ paśavas tava
english: "Defeating us in battle and humiliating us along with our kinsmen, the Trigārtas are driving away hundreds of thousands of cattle. O lord of men, pursue them — let not your livestock be lost!"

sanskrit: tac chrutvā nṛpatiḥ senāṃ matsyānāṃ samayojayat rathanāgāśvakalilāṃ pattidhvajasamākulām
english: Hearing that, the lord of the Matsyas marshaled his army — crowded with chariots, elephants, and horses, swarming with infantry and banners.

sanskrit: rājāno rājaputrāś ca tanutrāṇy atra bhejire bhānumanti vicitrāḥ sūpasevyāni bhāgaśaḥ
english: Kings and princes here put on their armor — radiant and variegated, finely crafted — each according to his own portion.

sanskrit: savajrāyasagarbhaṃ tu kavacaṃ taptakāñcanam virāṭasya priyo bhrātā śatānīko 'bhyahārayat
english: Śatānīka, the beloved brother of Virāṭa, brought armor reinforced with iron lightning-bolts and trimmed with heated gold.

sanskrit: sarvapārasavaṃ varma kalyāṇapaṭalaṃ dṛḍham śatānīkād avarajo madirāśvo 'bhyahārayat
english: Madirāśva, younger than Śatānīka, brought armor crafted entirely of excellent iron, covered with auspicious plates and very strong.

sanskrit: śatasūryaṃ śatāvartaṃ śatabindu śatākṣimat abhedyakalpaṃ matsyānāṃ rājā kavacam āharat
english: The king of the Matsyas himself brought his armor — blazing like a hundred suns, with a hundred swirling designs, a hundred spots, a hundred eyes, practically impenetrable.

sanskrit: utsedhe yasya padmāni śataṃ saugandhikāni ca suvarṇapṛṣṭhaṃ sūryābhaṃ sūryadatto 'bhyahārayat
english: Sūryadatta brought armor whose raised surfaces bore a hundred fragrant lotuses, with a golden back, gleaming like the sun.

sanskrit: dṛḍham āyasagarbhaṃ tu śvetaṃ varma śatākṣimat virāṭasya suto jyeṣṭho vīraḥ śaṅkho 'bhyahārayat
english: Śaṅkha, the eldest heroic son of Virāṭa, brought armor that was firm, reinforced with iron, white, and set with a hundred eyes.

sanskrit: śataśaś ca tanutrāṇi yathāsvāni mahārathāḥ yotsyamānābhyanahyanta devarūpāḥ prahāriṇaḥ
english: And the great warriors, god-like in form and fierce in attack, bound on their own armor by the hundreds as they prepared for battle.

sanskrit: sūpaskareṣu śubhreṣu mahatsu ca mahārathāḥ pṛthak kāñcanasaṃnāhān ratheṣv aśvān ayojayan
english: The great chariot-warriors yoked their horses, each with golden harnesses, separately to fine, bright, and great chariots.

sanskrit: sūryacandrapratīkāśo rathe divye hiraṇmayaḥ mahānubhāvo matsyasya dhvaja ucchiśriye tadā
english: The great standard of Matsya, resembling the sun and moon, was then raised high on his divine, golden chariot.

sanskrit: athānyān vividhākārān dhvajān hemavibhūṣitān yathāsvaṃ kṣatriyāḥ śūrā ratheṣu samayojayan
english: Then other brave Kṣatriyas fastened various kinds of gold-adorned banners each to his own chariot.

sanskrit: atha matsyo 'bravīd rājā śatānīkaṃ jaghanyajam kaṅkaballavagopālā dāmagranthiś ca vīryavān yudhyeyur iti me buddhir vartate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Then king Matsya said to the youngest, Śatānīka: "Kaṅka, Ballava, Gopāla, and the valiant Dāmagrantha — it is my intention that they should fight; of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: eteṣām api dīyantāṃ rathā dhvajapatākinaḥ kavacāni vicitrāḥ dṛḍhāni ca mṛdūni ca pratimuñcantu gātreṣu dīyantām āyudhāni ca
english: "Let chariots with banners and flags be given to these as well; let varied armor — both firm and flexible — be fastened on their bodies, and let weapons be given to them."

sanskrit: vīrāṅgarūpāḥ puruṣā nāgarājakaropamāḥ neme jātu na yudhyerann iti me dhīyate matiḥ
english: "Men of heroic build and resembling the trunks of elephant-lords — surely such men would never fail to fight. So runs my thinking."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu nṛpater vākyaṃ tvaritamānasaḥ śatānīkas tu pārthebhyo rathān rājan samādiśat sahadevāya rājñe ca bhīmāya nakulāya ca
english: Hearing the king's words and with his mind urgent, Śatānīka, O king, assigned chariots to the sons of Pṛthā — to Sahadeva, and to the king Yudhiṣṭhira, and to Bhīma, and to Nakula.

sanskrit: tān prahṛṣṭās tataḥ sūtā rājabhaktipuraskṛtāḥ nirdiṣṭān naradevena rathāñ śīghram ayojayan
english: Then the chariot-drivers, filled with joy and with devotion to the king foremost in their hearts, quickly yoked those chariots designated by the lord of men.

sanskrit: kavacāni vicitrāḥ dṛḍhāni ca mṛdūni ca virāṭaḥ prādiśad yāni teṣām akliṣṭakarmaṇām tāny āmucya śarīreṣu daṃśitās te paraṃtapāḥ
english: The varied armor, firm and flexible, which Virāṭa had issued for those tireless warriors — having fastened it on their bodies, those scorchers of foes were clad in armor.

sanskrit: tarasvinaś channarūpāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ virāṭam anvayuḥ paścāt sahitāḥ kurupuṃgavāḥ catvāro bhrātaraḥ śūrāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ satyavikramāḥ
english: Swift, disguised in form, all skilled in battle, the four heroic Pāṇḍava brothers, bulls among Kurus, of true valor, followed behind Virāṭa together.

sanskrit: bhīmāś ca mattamātaṅgāḥ prabhinnakaraṭāmukhāḥ kṣaranta iva jīmūtāḥ sudantāḥ ṣaṣṭihāyanāḥ
english: Fearsome elephants in rut, with ichor flowing from their temples, dripping like rain-clouds, with fine tusks, sixty years old —

sanskrit: svārūḍhā yuddhakuśalaiḥ śikṣitair hastisādibhiḥ rājānam anvayuḥ paścāc calanta iva parvatāḥ
english: — mounted by trained and battle-skilled elephant-drivers, followed the king from behind, moving like mountains.

sanskrit: viśāradānāṃ vaśyānāṃ hṛṣṭānāṃ cānuyāyinām aṣṭau rathasahasrāṇi daśa nāgaśatāni ca ṣaṣṭiś cāśvasahasrāṇi matsyānām abhiniryayuḥ
english: Eight thousand chariots, ten hundred elephants, and sixty thousand horses of the Matsyas, ready, obedient, joyful, and following, sallied forth.

sanskrit: tad anīkaṃ virāṭasya śuśubhe bharatarṣabha saṃprayātaṃ mahārāja ninīṣantaṃ gavāṃ padam
english: That army of Virāṭa shone brilliantly, O bull of the Bharatas, O great king, as it marched forth to retrieve the track of the cattle.

sanskrit: tad balāgryaṃ virāṭasya saṃprasthitam aśobhata dṛḍhāyudhajanākīrṇaṃ gajāśvarathasaṃkulam
english: That foremost army of Virāṭa set out and shone with splendor, crowded with men bearing firm weapons, thronged with elephants, horses, and chariots.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca niryāya nagarāc chūrā vyūḍhānīkāḥ prahāriṇaḥ trigartān aspṛśan matsyāḥ sūrye pariṇate sati
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Having sallied forth from the city, the brave, array-formed, fierce Matsyas came upon the Trigārtas as the sun was declining.

sanskrit: te trigartāś ca matsyāś ca saṃrabdhā yuddhadurmadāḥ anyonyam abhigarjanto goṣu gṛddhā mahābalāḥ
english: Those Trigārtas and Matsyas, enraged, frenzied for battle, roaring at one another, greedy for cattle, mighty in strength —

sanskrit: bhīmāś ca mattamātaṅgās tomarāṅkuśacoditāḥ grāmaṇīyaiḥ samārūḍhāḥ kuśalair hastisādibhiḥ
english: — and fearsome elephants in rut, goaded with iron darts and elephant-hooks, mounted by village leaders skilled as elephant-drivers —

sanskrit: teṣāṃ samāgamo ghoras tumulo lomaharṣaṇaḥ devāsurasamo rājann āsīt sūrye vilambati
english: — their encounter was terrible, tumultuous, hair-raising, equal to the battle of gods and Asuras, O king, as the sun slanted down.

sanskrit: udatiṣṭhad rajo bhaumaṃ na prajñāyata kiṃ cana pakṣiṇaś cāpatan bhūmau sainyena rajasāvṛtāḥ
english: Earthen dust arose and nothing could be discerned; birds fell to the ground, obscured by the dust of the armies.

sanskrit: iṣubhir vyatisaṃyadbhir ādityo 'ntaradhīyata khadyotair iva saṃyuktam antarikṣaṃ vyarājata
english: The sun was hidden by the crossing arrows; the sky shone as if filled with fireflies.

sanskrit: rukmapṛṣṭhāni cāpāni vyatiṣaktāni dhanvinām patatāṃ lokavīrāṇāṃ savyadakṣiṇam asyatām
english: The gold-backed bows of the bowmen intertwined as the world's heroes fell — shooting left and right.

sanskrit: rathā rathaiḥ samājagmuḥ pādātaiś ca padātayaḥ sādibhiḥ sādinaś caiva gajaiś cāpi mahāgajāḥ
english: Chariots clashed with chariots, foot-soldiers with foot-soldiers, cavalry with cavalry, and great elephants with great elephants.

sanskrit: asibhiḥ paṭṭiśaiḥ prāsaiḥ śaktibhis tomarair api saṃrabdhāḥ samare rājan nijaghnur itaretaram
english: With swords, battle-axes, lances, javelins, and iron darts, enraged in the battle, O king, they slew one another.

sanskrit: nighnantaḥ samare 'nyonyaṃ śūrāḥ parighabāhavaḥ na śekur abhisaṃrabdhāḥ śūrān kartuṃ parāṅmukhān
english: Slaying one another in battle, those heroes with club-like arms, furiously engaged, were unable to make the heroes turn their backs.

sanskrit: kḷptottaroṣṭhaṃ sunasaṃ kḷptakeśam alaṃkṛtam adṛśyata śiraś chinnaṃ rajodhvastaṃ sakuṇḍalam
english: A severed head was seen, with trimmed upper lip, fine nose, dressed hair, and adorned with earrings, covered with dust.

sanskrit: adṛśyaṃs tatra gātrāṇi śaraiś chinnāni bhāgaśaḥ śālaskandhanikāśāni kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahāmṛdhe
english: In that great slaughter of Kṣatriyas, limbs were seen, cut to pieces by arrows, resembling the trunks of Śāla trees.

sanskrit: nāgabhoganikāśaiś ca bāhubhiś candanokṣitaiḥ ākīrṇā vasudhā tatra śirobhiś ca sakuṇḍalaiḥ
english: The earth was strewn there with arms like serpents' coils, anointed with sandalwood paste, and with heads bearing earrings.

sanskrit: upaśāmyad rajo bhaumaṃ rudhireṇa prasarpatā kaśmalaṃ prāviśad ghoraṃ nirmaryādam avartata
english: The earthen dust was quelled by the spreading blood; a terrible, boundless faintness pervaded the field and raged without restraint.

sanskrit: śatānīkaḥ śataṃ hatvā viśālākṣaś catuḥśatam praviṣṭau mahatīṃ senāṃ trigartānāṃ mahārathau ārcchetāṃ bahusaṃrabdhau keśākeśi nakhānakhi
english: Śatānīka, having slain a hundred, and Viśālākṣa, having slain four hundred, both great warriors, plunged into the vast Trigārta army and grappled in fierce combat, hair gripping hair, nails tearing nails.

sanskrit: lakṣayitvā trigartānāṃ tau praviṣṭau rathavrajam jagmatuḥ sūryadattaś ca madirāśvaś ca pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Seeing those two plunge into the Trigārtas' chariot host, Sūryadatta and Madirāśva followed behind them.

sanskrit: virāṭas tatra saṃgrāme hatvā pañcaśatān rathān hayānāṃ ca śatāny atra hatvā pañca mahārathān
english: Virāṭa in that battle, having destroyed five hundred chariots and having slain here five hundred horses and five great warriors —
